feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: A Congressman wants his colleagues to pledge to accept election results
entry.summary: NPR's Ailsa Chang speaks with Rep. Josh Gottheimer, D-N.Y., on a bipartisan pledge he is co-leading to assure that fellow House members accept midterm elections results.

entry.title: Health Secretary Kennedy touts an initiative to study vaccine safety
entry.summary: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has established a new clinic at the National Institutes of Health to study vaccine injuries. It's part of a larger administration effort on vaccine safety.

entry.title: Study finds 194-year-old tortoise is 'aging more slowly than you would expect'
entry.summary: Researchers are studying the genome of the world's oldest land animal — a 194-year-old tortoise named Jonathan — to uncover secrets about his longevity.

entry.title: Flock is catching flak. Experts say other surveillance tools are more worrisome
entry.summary: AI-powered surveillance tools like Flock cameras have gotten a lot of media attention and public criticism, but there are many other lesser-known tools being deployed by local police departments.

entry.title: Global guidelines for sharing illness information date back to the 1850s
entry.summary: International Health Regulations mandate that countries share information about illness that may affect people beyond their borders. It's being put to the test after a Russian plague researcher died.

entry.title: ICE has quietly used this warehouse as a detention facility all summer, neighbors say
entry.summary: Throughout the summer, rumors have been bubbling in North New Jersey that ICE has quietly been using a warehouse as a detention center. NPR investigated.

entry.title: As crypto and prediction markets expand, their regulator shrinks
entry.summary: Even as the agency is tasked with drawing up new rules for crypto and prediction markets, its staffing and enforcement actions have dropped precipitously during the second Trump administration.

entry.title: Author Tomi Adeyemi contends with reality in her new book, 'The Siren'
entry.summary: The author Tomi Adeyemi has written fantasy all her life. Now, she has a new book out titled The Siren, which takes place in the real world.

entry.title: Republicans and Democrats find a unifying target: Pharmacy benefit managers
entry.summary: Republicans and Democrats, both patients and politicians, seem united in their disdain for the healthcare companies known as pharmacy benefit managers. Tennessee and Arkansas are regulating now them.

entry.title: The WHO seeks more details on the death of a plague research lab employee in Russia
entry.summary: The World Health Organization says it wants more information on what caused the death of an employee at a Russian plague research lab. Russia says the woman died of pneumonia of unknown origin.
